name: Joint Corner Descent for Rooted Factors and Ordinary Obstructions
statement: Starting from either a rooted factor or an ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness, repeatedly delete a nonterminal corner and minor-minimize the residual rooted or ordinary failure. Cardinality decreases strictly, and the process ends either at a rooted factor whose root is its only geometric corner or at a cornerless ample pc-minimal obstruction. A rooted deletion with a corner-peelable remainder stays in the rooted branch; a nonpeelable remainder enters the ordinary branch, which is then permanent.
proof: Deleting a nonroot corner from a rooted factor preserves ampleness and rooted failure. A positive remainder admits rooted minor descent; a negative remainder contains an ordinary pc-minimal obstruction. Deleting a corner from an ordinary nonpeelable ample family remains nonpeelable, since any peeling of the remainder could be prefixed by that corner, so ordinary minor-minimization can continue. Every step begins with a deletion, forcing termination with exactly the stated corner conditions.
